newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon orders crackdown on Shi'ite cleric.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon orders crackdown on Shi'ite cleric.

text.p: The Lebanese government has ordered the army and security forces to take tough measures against leaders of a civil disobedience campaign.

The cabinet, in a session late on Wednesday, made the decision to crack down on a civil disobedience campaign led by former Hizbollah leader Sheikh Sobi Tufaili after an unlicensed radio station run by the radical Shi'ite cleric threatened reprisals against any prosecution.

President Elias Hrawi read a security report stating that the radio station had been calling on its followers to defy the government, which has already threatened legal action against Tufaili's "hunger revolt".
Hrawi said the broadcast threatened that thousands of would-be martyrs were ready for revenge and warned of a "sea of blood".

The Lebanese president did not directly name Tufaili, a fiery cleric who has threatened to lay siege to the palaces of Lebanese leaders if they do not take swift action to ease poverty in Lebanon, but the security report did name him.
Tufaili, who condemns Hizbollah's current leaders as too soft, no longer holds an official post in the group but enjoys a following from its most radical members.
He has become a potent force in Lebanese politics but Lebanese analysts question his ability to press ahead with a threat to spread the civil disobedience campaign across Lebanon.
